title: The normal integral case
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in
$K$. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $K$, let $S'$
be an affine, integral and normal $K$-scheme with algebraically
closed function field $L$, set $X'=X\times_KS'$,
$Y=X'\times_{S'}\Spec(L)$, and let $h:Y\to X'$ be the projection.
Then $R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}=0$ for all $q>0$
and all $d\mid n$. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1I), final
reduction.)

proof.text: Write $S'=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The whole affine open of the integral scheme $S'$ is nonempty, so [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies its function field $L$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ and makes $B$ a domain. By [lem-kun-algebra-union], take $I$ to be the set of finitely generated $K$-subalgebras $B_i\subseteq B$, ordered by inclusion, with union $B$. Form the small directed preorder $J$ of pairs $(i,g)$, $0\ne g\in B_i$, with $(i,g)\le(i',g')$ exactly when $B_i\subseteq B_{i'}$ and $g$ is a unit in $(B_{i'})_{g'}$. By [lem-kun-colim-of-localizations], the canonical transition maps are defined, $J$ is filtered, and $L=\varinjlim_J(B_i)_g$. In particular this indexing family is nonempty; $(K,1)$ is an index.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0F1I (lemma-punctual-base-change), final paragraph of proof

proof.text: For $j=(i,g)$ put $S_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)_g$, $X_j=X\times_K S_j$, and $Y_j=X\times_K U_j$, with projections $f_j:X_j\to S_j$, $e_j:Y_j\to U_j$, $g_j:U_j\to S_j$, and $h_j:Y_j\to X_j$. These are compatible cartesian squares, by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. The repeated diagram $j\mapsto B_i$ also has colimit $B$: a compatible cocone sends $b\in B_i$ to its image at $(i,1)$; a common upper bound of any two pairs proves this independent of the representing stage and pair, and proves that addition and multiplication are preserved. This gives exactly one ring map from $B$, extending every cocone map. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] gives $S'=\varprojlim_JS_j$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L=\varprojlim_JU_j$, and says their transition maps are affine. For any test scheme $T$, compatible maps $T\to X_j$ are exactly a single map $T\to X$ together with compatible maps $T\to S_j$, all over $K$: the $X$-components agree because any two indices have a common upper bound. By the fibre-product universal property they are exactly maps $T\to X\times_KS'$. The same argument gives $\varprojlim_JY_j=X\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L=Y$. The limit maps agree with the prescribed $h,e,f,g$ by their projections. Each transition $X_{j'}\to X_j$ (respectively $Y_{j'}\to Y_j$) is the base change of $S_{j'}\to S_j$ (respectively $U_{j'}\to U_j$), hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. This constructs all four limits rather than assuming their existence.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0F1I (lemma-punctual-base-change), final paragraph of proof

proof.text: The schemes $S_j$ and $U_j$ are of finite type over $K$: if $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate $B_i$, then $b_1,\ldots,b_r,1/g$ generate $(B_i)_g$, directly by the description of localization as fractions. This is finite generation in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and gives finite type of the two affine schemes by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $g_j$ is the principal-open immersion. Since both schemes are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $g_j$ affine. It is therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Thus these are finite-type open-immersion squares, with the other factor the given finite-type scheme $X$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0F1I (lemma-punctual-base-change), final paragraph of proof

proof.text: It suffices to consider positive divisors: if the notation $d\mid n$ allows signed integer divisors, then $d\ne0$ since $n\ge1$, and $d\mathbf Z=|d|\mathbf Z$ gives the identical quotient group. Fix a positive divisor $d$ of $n$, and put $M=\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ and $F_j=\underline M$ on $U_{j,\mathrm{Et}}$, using [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Since $n=d a$ for an integer $a$, $nM=0$ and $M$ is a $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-module by reduction modulo $d$. Hence $F_j$ has torsion stalks of orders invertible in $K$ by [lem-kun-zn-sheaf-invertible-orders], used with the given $n$ (there is no need to change the annihilator to $d$). Use the canonical constant-sheaf pullback isomorphisms of [lem-kun-pullback-constant] as the transition maps; these obey identity and composition, since on the constant presheaf they send each value $m$ to the same value $m$, and sheafification preserves these equalities. The same identifications make every $p_j^{-1}F_j$ on $\operatorname{Spec}L$ equal to $\underline M$ with identity transition maps. Their colimit is $\underline M$: by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] a cocone to any sheaf $G$ consists of one map $\underline M\to G$, since a common upper bound forces any two components to agree. Also $e_j^{-1}F_j=\underline M$ on $Y_j$, and $e^{-1}\underline M=\underline M$ on $Y$, by the same pullback lemma.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0F1I (lemma-punctual-base-change), final paragraph of proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0f1h] to $g_j:U_j\hookrightarrow S_j$, the other factor $X$, and $F_j$, for every $j$. It gives the canonical derived exchange $f_j^{-1}Rg_{j,*}F_j\to Rh_{j,*}e_j^{-1}F_j$ as an isomorphism. Use abelian-group coefficients, equivalently $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, throughout. The sheaf $F_j[0]$ is bounded below; [sk-def-exchange] identifies the restriction of the unbounded exchange with the bounded below mate, with the same unit and counit. By [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology], its degree-$q$ cohomology is precisely the canonical map $f_j^{-1}R^qg_{j,*}F_j\to R^qh_{j,*}e_j^{-1}F_j$. A functor carries an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse morphisms. Thus this higher-direct-image map is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$, as required in the next step.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0F1I (lemma-punctual-base-change), final paragraph of proof

proof.text:
Fix $q>0$. Apply [lem-kun-0ezt] to the directed system of cartesian squares constructed above. The index is a set; all four systems have affine transitions; each $g_j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; and the compatible $F_j$ are torsion abelian sheaves with colimit $F=\underline M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}L$. The preceding step supplies the required isomorphism at each stage for this fixed $q$. The resulting limit base-change map is therefore an isomorphism
$$f^{-1}R^qg_*\underline M\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qh_*e^{-1}\underline M=R^qh_*\underline M,$$
where $f:X'\to S'$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to S'$ are the original projections.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0F1I (lemma-punctual-base-change), final paragraph of proof

proof.text: An algebraically closed field has no proper finite algebraic extension: a minimal polynomial of any element of such an extension is irreducible and, having a root in the base field, must be linear. Thus the hypothesis on $L$ in [def-weil-algebraic-closure] implies it is separably closed in [def-kun-separably-closed]. Apply the consequent clause of [lem-kun-0ezp] to the morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to S'$ and the abelian sheaf $\underline M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}L$. It gives $R^qg_*\underline M=0$ for $q>0$. The exact inverse-image functor of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] preserves the zero object (as a finite limit), so the left side of the isomorphism in the preceding step is zero. Hence $R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}=0$. The choices of $q>0$ and positive $d\mid n$ were arbitrary, proving all clauses.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in
$K$. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $K$, let $S'$
be an affine, integral and normal $K$-scheme with algebraically
closed function field $L$, set $X'=X\times_KS'$,
$Y=X'\times_{S'}\Spec(L)$, and let $h:Y\to X'$ be the projection.
Then $R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}=0$ for all $q>0$
and all $d\mid n$.

proof.text:
Write $S'=\Spec(B)$, so that $L$ is the fraction field of $B$.
By [lem-kun-algebra-union] write $B=\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i$ as the
union of its finite type $K$-subalgebras $B_i$. Let $J$ be the
set of pairs $(i,g)$ with $i\in I$ and $g\in B_i$ nonzero,
ordered by $(i',g')\ge(i,g)$ if and only if $B_i\subset B_{i'}$
and $g$ maps to an invertible element of $(B_{i'})_{g'}$. Then
$L=\varinjlim_{(i,g)\in J}(B_i)_g$ by
[lem-kun-colim-of-localizations]. For $j=(i,g)\in J$ set
$S_j=\Spec(B_i)$ and $U_j=\Spec((B_i)_g)$. Then the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}\\
S'&\longleftarrow&\Spec(L)
\end{array}
\qquad\text{is the limit of}\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}
X\times_KS_j&\xleftarrow{\;h_j\;}&X\times_KU_j\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}\\
S_j&\longleftarrow&U_j
\end{array}
$$

by [lem-kun-fibre-product-limits] (limits and fibre products
commute) and [lem-kun-colim-of-localizations]: the rings $(B_i)_g$
have filtered colimit $L$, so their spectra have limit $\Spec(L)$, and
the resulting maps exhibit the diagram $S'\leftarrow\Spec(L)$ as the
limit of the diagrams $S_j\leftarrow U_j$. Thus we may
apply [lem-kun-0ezt] to see that it suffices to prove that the
exchange morphisms (of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]) hold in the
diagrams on the right. Each right-hand diagram is the diagram of
[lem-kun-0f1h] for the open immersion $j:U_j\to S_j$ of finite
type $K$-schemes and the scheme $X$ of finite type over $K$,
applied to the sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}$, a sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$-modules whose stalks are $d$-torsion, with
$d\mid n$ invertible in $K$, hence of orders invertible in $K$
by [lem-kun-zn-sheaf-invertible-orders].
Hence [lem-kun-0f1h] gives

$$
(X\times_KS_j\to S_j)^{-1}R^q(U_j\to S_j)_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}
\;\cong\;R^qh_{j,*}\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}
$$

for all $q\ge0$. Passing to the limit with
[lem-kun-0ezt] we obtain

$$
(X'\to S')^{-1}R^q(\Spec(L)\to S')_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}
\;\cong\;R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}
$$

for all $q$. But $\Spec(L)$ is integral and normal with
algebraically closed (hence separably closed) function field, so
$R^q(\Spec(L)\to S')_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}=0$ for
$q>0$ by [lem-kun-0ezp]. Hence
$R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}=0$ for $q>0$, as
desired.

Read every cited node's statement and Stacks 0F1I (etale-cohomology.tex l.20596-20703), 0EZT (l.16409), 0F1H (l.20402) and 0EZP (l.14368). Steps 1-2: B is a domain with Frac B=L; J is filtered with L=colim; colim_J B_i=B is proved by an explicit cocone argument; the four limits are built by the test-scheme property, not assumed, so dropping lem-kun-fibre-product-limits is justified; transitions are affine by base change. Step 3: finite type, principal open immersion and qcqs, which are the 0F1H and 0EZT hypotheses. Step 4: Z/d is a Z/n-module, so orders are invertible; the constant system is compatible with colimit Z/d. Step 5: 0F1H gives the def-kun-unbounded-exchange iso; sk-def-exchange restricts it to D+ with Lambda=Z, and lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology turns it into the usual R^q base-change map, so the coefficient category is unchanged. Step 6: every 0EZT hypothesis holds, including cartesian squares by pasting. Step 7: algebraically closed implies separably closed; the field clause of 0EZP (source Spec L) and exact inverse image give 0. Edge cases d=1, X empty, S'=Spec L and non-noetherian B all hold. Dropping K algebraically closed (Stacks has it at this point of the proof) is harmless and does not weaken the item. No cycle; the only citer is lem-kun-0f1i.
